clue.text: Inner ear of my horse without name

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside' means one part sits round another

blocks.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A strange anatomical query about the inner ear of somebody's horse, minus a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ear' is the misdirection: not the hearing organ but an ear of corn. 'Cor!' is a British exclamation like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the woody central core of a maize ear, so it is literally what lies inside the ear.

clue.text: See 16
Respect from cleric shortly before church

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter
one part comes ahead of the other in the answer

blocks.note: a reverend is a member of the clergy; the last letter is dropped
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Respect shown by a clergyman just before a service.
explanation.walkthrough: REVEREND clipped to REVEREN, then CE, gives REVERENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect or veneration, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 1 under 100 for 99?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means coming lower, so after the other part

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the digit written as a word

explanation.surface: A numerical puzzle: one below a hundred makes ninety-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The arithmetic reading (100 minus 1 is 99) is the false path. A 99 is a British ice cream: soft-serve in a cone with a chocolate Flake stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A 99 is an ice cream served in a wafer cone, so the cone is an example-style hint, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Welsh friend with brains capturing English coastal position

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so one part closes round another

blocks.note: bach is a Welsh term of affection, like 'dear' or 'mate'
E is the abbreviation for English
the head holds the brains; 'use your head'

explanation.surface: A clever Welsh pal taking an English seaside spot, like a holiday land-grab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bach' is Welsh for dear or mate, a term of affection, not the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachhead is a military foothold seized on an enemy shore, a strategic position on the coast.

clue.text: Mister Bob Hope

blocks.note: a bob was an old British shilling, abbreviated s
a prayer is a hope or wish

explanation.surface: Reads as a polite reference to the comedian Bob Hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title for Bob Hope, but it means something that mists. A bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A mister is a device that sends out a fine spray, so it is a kind of sprayer, read literally as one who mists.

clue.text: Excessive energy used in action

indicators.note: something used in a thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
a step is a move or action, as in 'take steps'

explanation.surface: A complaint that too much effort went into some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes into STEP to give STEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for unreasonably high, as of a price, so it means excessive in that colloquial sense.

clue.text: Governor degenerate with a gun sent heavenwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up towards heaven means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: to rot is to degenerate or decay
taken as written
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A corrupt state governor with a gun, sent to meet his maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' looks like an adjective for the governor, but it is a verb meaning decay. ROT, A and LUGER together run upwards to give REGULATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor in engineering is a device controlling speed or flow, which is exactly what a regulator does.

clue.text: Bridge player with yen for brewing agent

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
the four players in bridge are North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A card player with a hankering for a beer-making job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' poses as a longing; it is the currency. Y joins EAST, with the player coming second despite being named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol, the active agent in brewing beer.

clue.text: Is cutting horribly hard salad ingredient

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it
done horribly, the letters end up in a mangled order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that some salad vegetable is awfully hard to slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as slicing the vegetable; it means going into the middle of the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp peppery root commonly sliced raw into salads.

clue.text: Profit from commercial vehicle say at back

indicators.note: to go back is to run the opposite way, right to left

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
a van is a vehicle
e.g. means 'for example', i.e. 'say'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Earning money from an advertising van, perhaps with a message on its rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At back' reads like a position on the van; instead 'say at' as a pair is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit as a noun means gain or benefit, and advantage is a benefit or favourable gain.

clue.text: Delighted to receive new pancreas?

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one part holds another

blocks.note: glad means pleased or delighted
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A patient thrilled about getting a transplanted pancreas.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAD takes in N. The question mark flags that the pancreas is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is an organ that secretes insulin and digestive juices, making it an instance of a gland.

clue.text: Staple feature of horror writer Vidal

blocks.note: first meaning: blood spilt in violence, as in slasher films
second meaning: the first name of the American novelist and essayist Vidal

explanation.surface: Seems to say a writer called Vidal was a staple of horror fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about a horror writer; it splits after 'horror' into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt blood is a gruesome mainstay of horror films, and the American author Vidal was christened with this first name.

clue.text: Sausages, cold, a hospital ordered

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a sequence, here a new one

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's order of cold sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a hospital placing an order, but it is the rearrangement signal for the letters of the other three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipolatas are small thin British pork sausages, often served with roast turkey.

clue.text: Matchless leg cut breaking duck

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
to pare is to cut or trim
a duck in cricket is a score of zero

explanation.surface: A cricket image: an unrivalled leg-side shot that ends a batter's run without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket supplies two conventions: the leg side is also called the on side, and a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil comes from French for 'without equal', so it means unrivalled or having no match.

clue.text: Greek commander soon brought about plucky Ilium's end

indicators.note: a word's end is its final letter
to be brought about something is to be put around it

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means brave or plucky
the last letter of Ilium

explanation.surface: A Greek general who will shortly bring about the fall of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is another name for Troy, which fits the Greek commander's story; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, led the Greek forces against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Weeping willow in centre covers ornate May arch

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is wanted, its two central letters
something ornate is elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged
to cover something is to go round it

blocks.note: the two middle letters of willow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weeping willow draped over a decorated archway at a May festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeping willow' looks like a single tree; 'Weeping' alone is the definition. The two Ls go around the rearranged MAY ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal relates to tears or crying, from Latin lacrima, so it is a formal adjective for tearful.

clue.text: What causes daughter to appear in military ceremony?

definitions.text: What causes daughter to appear in military ceremony?

blocks.note: surface reading: a formal military parade, such as the one at Buckingham Palace
setter's reading: rearranging the letters of a two-word phrase for a sentry produces the word for a female child

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why someone's daughter suddenly turns up at a military parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: 'changing' the letters of THE GUARD gives DAUGHTER. The ceremony is the famous sentry handover outside Buckingham Palace in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal ceremonial handover between outgoing and incoming sentries at royal palaces, a well-known military ritual.

clue.text: Train trip on time after Euston evacuated

indicators.note: emptied of contents, the word keeps only its outer letters
one part follows the other in the answer

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Euston
a tour is a trip
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A railway journey running on schedule after London's Euston station is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is not a railway train but a retinue; Euston, a London terminus, is just there to be emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can mean a body of followers or attendants, and an entourage is such a retinue around an important person.

clue.text: Old god shelters unknown ship for latest 27 Across 26 Down

indicators.note: to shelter something is to enclose and protect it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
deus is Latin for god
in algebra, y is an unknown quantity
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An ancient god hides a mystery vessel for a director's newest film hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points across the grid to NOLAN and HERO: Christopher Nolan's latest film is The Odyssey. Deus is Latin, not a Greek name.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Nolan's 2026 film The Odyssey adapts Homer's epic, whose wandering protagonist is the king of Ithaca.

clue.text: Earwax regularly removed in long period

indicators.note: taking out every other letter leaves the alternate ones

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of earwax

explanation.surface: Earwax being cleaned out routinely over a long stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' suggests routine cleaning, but it means at even intervals: drop the second, fourth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is an extended span of history marked by some feature, a long stretch of time.

clue.text: Honoured in Germany, EC spoke at length

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
taken as written
to orate is to make a long formal speech

explanation.surface: A European Commission speaker is honoured in Germany after a long address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Germany' reads as a place; 'in' only links, and Germany gives its car-plate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be decorated is to be awarded a medal or honour, as a soldier is for bravery.

clue.text: Singer Tyler so pretty?

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the Welsh singer of 'Total Eclipse of the Heart'
second meaning: a Scottish word for attractive

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain singer called Tyler is good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hedges the Scots word: it is regional, not everyday English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh rock singer Tyler's first name doubles as the Scottish adjective for attractive or fair.

clue.text: See 16
This emerging from bulb lit up explosively

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A light bulb blowing as it is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' reads as a light bulb, which suits 'lit up'; it is the flower bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips grow from bulbs planted in autumn, so it is a flower that emerges from one.

clue.text: Relative going topless, free from bonds

indicators.note: losing its top means losing the first letter in a down entry

blocks.note: an auntie is a relative; its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A relative stripping off and casting off restraints.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE loses its A to give UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo knots or ropes, releasing someone from bonds.

clue.text: American weakling with American SEALS at first

indicators.note: the first letter alone is wanted

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
US is short for American
the first letter of SEALS

explanation.surface: A feeble American alongside tough US Navy special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: SEALS are the US Navy's elite commandos, a pointed contrast to a weakling. 'With' is a piece here, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wuss is American slang for a timid or feeble person, a coward.

clue.text: An Achilles in the room?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the following words

blocks.note: spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Recalls the phrase 'an elephant in the room', swapped for a Greek warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoing 'elephant in the room' makes the clue feel like an idiom; the letters straddle two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the great warrior of the Trojan War, the model of a Greek legendary champion.

clue.text: Film director in Frognal once retired

to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A filmmaker who used to live in Frognal before retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Frognal is a street and district in Hampstead, north London, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Nolan is the British director of Inception, Oppenheimer and The Odyssey.

clue.text: Abstemious, but consumed with rage

blocks.note: a temper is a fit of rage
consumed food: ate

explanation.surface: Someone moderate in habits who is nonetheless eaten up with anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed with rage' is an idiom for furious; split it and the eating word follows the anger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means restrained in eating and drinking, and temperate likewise means moderate in indulgence.

clue.text: Outgoing submarine docks in Devon river

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the Exe flows through Devon to Exeter
submarine pens are sheltered docks for subs

explanation.surface: A submarine departing from its moorings on a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' looks like a departing sub, but it is a noun: money going out. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, as a noun, is money spent, usually in the plural, and an expense is a cost incurred.

clue.text: Insoles designed for Leah Williamson?

indicators.note: something designed is newly shaped, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Custom shoe inserts made for a famous footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Leah Williamson captained England's women's football team, nicknamed the Lionesses, to the 2022 European title.
